clusters.title: Context chip's accessible name: LAN (kit) vs Context: LAN (Vue)

spec.says: suggested context label (LAN, VPN or none), editable; silent on the accessible name

kit.says: caption Context, then a menu button named by its content: 'LAN', or '—' offline

vue.says: aria-label 'Context: {label}'

evidence.notes: Vue's name contains the visible text (WCAG 2.5.3). '—' alone says nothing about what the menu changes.

clusters.title: Enter and Esc hints inside the main button's accessible name

spec.says: Desktop layouts show the Enter and Escape hints on the button; silent on the accessible name

kit.says: <kbd>Enter</kbd> inside the button, so its name is 'Start test Enter'

vue.says: <kbd aria-hidden="true">, name 'Start test'

evidence.notes: aria-keyshortcuts is the ARIA way to expose the shortcut; neither side uses it.

clusters.title: Polite live region: inside the Speed test section (kit) vs directly in main (Vue)

spec.says: a separate, visually hidden polite live region announces the phase and the rate; silent on its DOM position

kit.says: role=status aria-live=polite, visually hidden, inside the gauge in <section aria-label="Speed test">

vue.says: <LiveRegions> directly in <main>, before the section

evidence.notes: Placement changes nothing announced, but it makes the harness mis-pair notices in many scenarios.

clusters.title: Notices wrapped in a labelled list (Vue) vs bare notices (kit)

spec.says: silent on a list wrapper

kit.says: N(...) renders bare divs with role status or alert

vue.says: <ul :aria-label="$t('notices.label')"> with one <li> per notice

evidence.notes: A labelled list tells screen-reader users how many notices there are; the kit's bare notices are simpler. The wrapper also shifts the notices' paths.

clusters.title: Stop during idle latency with enough pings: kit keeps a partial result, Vue returns to Idle

spec.says: returns to Idle when 'nothing was measured yet (stopped during info or idle latency with too few samples)'; fewer than 5 samples → idle latency unavailable

kit.says: cancel at 12 of 20 pings keeps idle latency and jitter as 'Partial — stopped early', Run again, a result bar

vue.says: an interrupted idle phase returns null, so no result and the screen returns to Idle

evidence.notes: The spec implies 5+ samples give a partial result (kit), but screens.md:41 ties Keep to a finished phase. Needs a spec clarification, then an engine change.

clusters.title: Error before any phase finished: kit offers Download JSON in a result bar, Vue shows none

spec.says: If no phase completed, there is nothing to keep

kit.says: error-early: result bar 'Partial results are not saved · Download the JSON to keep them.' with Download JSON

vue.says: <ResultBar v-if="... run.result.value !== null"> (no result, no bar)

clusters.title: Result status time of day: kit's literal 24-hour sample vs Intl in the active locale

spec.says: Dates and times use Intl.DateTimeFormat with the active locale and the browser's time zone

kit.says: saved: { time: '15:26:40' } (literal sample)

vue.says: Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { timeStyle: 'medium' }) → 3:26:40 PM for en

evidence.notes: The kit's literal cannot carry a locale. Side note: the active locale is the language only, so en-GB users get 12-hour time too.

decision.rationale: Vue follows i18n-a11y §1.3 (Intl with the active locale, 12-hour for en); the kit's 15:26:40 is a literal sample with no locale.

clusters.title: Edit link to Settings in the settings summary (v0.2)

spec.says: The settings summary shows the effective values without an Edit link

kit.says: Edit, unconditional, leads to Settings

vue.says: v0.1 has no Settings screen, so there is no Edit link

clusters.title: Settings and History in the navigation (v0.2 screens), with the tab widths they cause

spec.says: v0.1 has no Settings screen: navigation shows Test and About; Settings is Spec'd (v0.2)

kit.says: v0.1 scope filters only 'history', and About never receives v01

vue.says: items = [test, about]

evidence.notes: Includes the narrow tab widths (2 tabs in Vue, 3-4 in the kit).

clusters.title: Slow scenarios: the kit suggests VPN for the private address 10.8.0.6, the spec and demo LAN

spec.says: both client addresses are private, so the suggested label is LAN for each; suggestedLabel is VPN for cgnat, LAN for private

kit.says: sel = ctxSel || (slow ? 'VPN' : 'LAN'); Client IP slow ? '10.8.0.6' : '192.168.1.42'

vue.says: addressClass: 'private', suggestedLabel: 'LAN' for every link

evidence.notes: The kit's 10.8.0.6 with VPN contradicts the address-class mapping; the spec records LAN for the demo on purpose.

decision.rationale: The spec wins: wire-protocol §5 maps a private address to LAN and frontend.md §9 records LAN for the demo on purpose. The kit's VPN on 10.8.0.6 contradicts the mapping, so the difference is kept until the export fixes it.

actions.what: design-system-upstream.md: the kit's slow client should use a CGNAT address (e.g. 100.101.4.17) if it suggests VPN, or suggest LAN for 10.8.0.6 (wire-protocol §5).

clusters.title: Page host in the header: the kit's speed.home.lan vs the demo's own origin

spec.says: Server name ... in the persistent header with the page's host

kit.says: host: this.props.host || 'speed.home.lan'

vue.says: const host = window.location.host

evidence.notes: Both follow the spec; the value is where the page is served from. Normalise each side's own page host in the content capture (web/parity/side.ts, capture.ts).

decision.rationale: Both sides show the page's own host as the spec asks; the value depends only on where each page is served from, so the harness treats each side's own host as equal.

actions.what: Replace each side's own page host (prototype speed.home.lan, Vue the demo origin's host) with one token in the content capture before normalisation; unit test; a bullet with its reason in demo-parity.md § What It Compares.

clusters.title: Border colour of a 1px transparent border compared with a 0-width border

spec.says: says nothing on borders of icon or ghost buttons

kit.says: .btn{border:1px solid transparent}

vue.says: ghost and default variants have no border (0 width, currentColor)

evidence.notes: A transparent 1px border and a 0-width border render the same; web/parity/compare/style.ts applies() compares the colour because the kit's side has width.

decision.rationale: A 1px transparent border and a 0-width border render the same; their colours are not a difference.

actions.what: web/parity/compare/style.ts: skip a border colour when one side's border is transparent and the other side's has no width; unit test; note the skip in demo-parity.md.

clusters.title: Data used, duration and packet loss: one card inside Results (kit) vs three tiles after it (Vue)

match.detail: ^(link "Why\?"|text "Data used|text "… Idle latency — Jitter — Test Data used)

spec.says: v0.1 metrics: download, upload, idle latency, jitter, data used, duration and the packet loss slot; silent on grouping

kit.says: one 'Test' card (Data used, Duration, Packet loss with Not measured and Why?) inside <section aria-label="Results">

vue.says: Results section holds the main tiles; data used, duration and packet loss are three tiles in an unlabelled div after it

evidence.notes: Vue's inline reason 'Browsers can't see packet loss over TCP' plus a docs link is what the spec asks for; the kit hides the reason in a title tooltip.

clusters.title: Base typography: the kit's body 14px and line-height normal vs Tailwind preflight's 16px/1.5

spec.says: visuals come from the export (docs/README.md#precedence)

kit.says: body { font-size: var(--text-base) } and no line-height anywhere, so line-height stays normal

vue.says: no base text size (16px) and html { line-height: 1.5 }; text-sm adds leading calc(1.25/.875) on the export's 13px

evidence.notes: One root cause under ~295 differences: header items, brand, buttons, notices, headings, links. Fix: kit's base size and line-height normal globally, then a full re-run.

vue.says: text-(length:--text-3xl) (24px) leading-[1.2] at every width

clusters.title: Button anatomy: kit .btn/.btn.sm sizes and secondary fill vs shadcn sizes and unmapped secondary tokens

match.path: ^main > button "(Download JSON|Retry|LICENSE file in the repository|Cancel|Source repository|Deployment docs|Reload)"

spec.says: visuals from the export; shadcn defaults only where it is silent

kit.says: .btn 34px, 0 14px, gap 8px, semibold; .btn.sm 28px, 0 10px, 12px; .btn.secondary surface-3 fill, border-default border; sizes sm 28 / md 34 / lg 38

vue.says: shadcn sm h-8 px-3 font-medium, default h-9 px-4; --color-secondary and --color-accent are not mapped, so secondary renders unstyled and outline's light border is near-black currentColor

evidence.notes: The unmapped tokens come from tokens.md's Tailwind mapping copied verbatim; mapping them in index.css needs an upstream note.
